cards.q: Match each NDT method with what it finds.
pairs: Surface and near-surface flaws in ferromagnetic steel
Surface cracks and conductivity changes in conductive metals
Internal flaws with volume, such as porosity
cards.why: Pick the method for the material, the flaw type and where it lies.

cards.q: What can dye penetrant testing not find?
options: Flaws that do not break the surface
Porosity that is open to the surface
cards.why: Penetrant has to soak into an opening, so subsurface flaws are invisible to it.

cards.q: On which material does magnetic particle testing not work?
cards.why: MT needs a ferromagnetic material. Austenitic stainless (and aluminium, titanium) are not, so PT or ET is used instead.

options: Acceptance quality levels for welded joints
cards.why: It sets the levels, training, experience and exams. PCN, run by BINDT, is the UK's scheme under it.

cards.q: Match each NDT level with its role.
pairs: Carries out tests to written instructions
Sets up, tests and interprets to standards; writes instructions
Writes and approves procedures, and takes technical responsibility
cards.why: Each level can do everything below it.
Aerospace uses employer-based certification to NAS 410 / EN 4179 rather than central schemes like PCN.

cards.q: Sound travels at 1480 m/s in water. The water path is {w} mm. How long after the pulse does the front-surface echo arrive, in µs?
cards.why: There and back: $t = \frac{2d}{v}$, with d in mm and v in m/s giving ms; × 1000 for µs.

cards.q: A {t} mm steel plate (5920 m/s) is tested in water (1480 m/s). What is the shortest water path that keeps the second front-surface echo beyond the back wall, in mm?
cards.why: The water path's transit time must exceed the steel's: water path ≥ thickness × $\frac{1480}{5920}$, about a quarter of the steel thickness.

cards.q: A probe focuses at {f} mm in water. The water path to steel is {wp} mm. Roughly how deep in the steel does it focus, in mm?
cards.why: Refraction at the surface shortens the rest of the focal length by the velocity ratio: about a quarter in steel.

cards.q: A scanner wheel of circumference {circ} mm carries an encoder with {lines} lines per turn, read in quadrature (4 counts per line). Data is taken every {s} mm. How many counts is that between samples?
cards.why: Counts per turn = {lines} × 4; per mm = that ÷ {circ} mm; × {s} mm per sample.

cards.q: A scanner fires {prf} pulses a second and needs one A-scan every {st} mm along the scan. What is the fastest scan speed, in mm/s?
cards.why: One pulse per sample point: speed = pulse rate × sample spacing. Averaging or several channels share the pulses and cut it.

options: A single A-scan trace from one point
A plan view of a gate's reading by position
A cross-section along the beam's path
cards.why: Each pixel is one position, coloured by what the gate saw there. B-scans are the cross-sections.

cards.q: What does a phased array probe do?
options: Fires elements with delays to steer and focus
Uses two separate probes facing each other
Sends one very long pulse into the part
Measures the temperature of the part
cards.why: Changing the delay law changes the beam's angle and focus electronically, so one probe does many angles.

cards.q: How does TOFD size a crack?
options: From the colour of the C-scan
cards.why: Tip diffraction timing gives height accurately, largely independent of the crack's orientation or reflectivity.

cards.q: Elements {p} mm apart steer a beam {a}° in steel (5920 m/s). What delay is needed between neighbouring elements, in nanoseconds?
cards.why: $\Delta t = \frac{p \sin\theta}{v}$: each element fires a little later so the wavefront tilts.

cards.q: Why are lower frequencies often used on thick composites?
options: Sound is faster in composites than steel
cards.why: Resin absorbs and fibres scatter; lower frequencies get through, at some cost to resolution.

cards.q: In a CFRP laminate (about 3000 m/s), an echo arrives {t} µs after the front surface. How deep is the reflector, in mm?
cards.why: Depth = velocity × time ÷ 2; m/s × µs ÷ 1000 gives mm, then halve.

cards.q: In a through-transmission C-scan of a composite, how does a delamination show?
options: A bright spot, where more sound gets through
Low amplitude: the gap blocks the sound
An echo halfway through the part
It does not show on a C-scan
cards.why: Two probes either side: anything with air in it, such as a delamination or porosity, stops the sound reaching the receiver.
